done_when: forge land and forge close never stop just because checks are queued: land keeps waiting, and close's wait line says plainly that the checks are queued, for how long, and that the shared runners may be busy or no runner may match the runner setting; only forge doctor reports a likely missing runner, and only when no job of this repo needing that runner has run in the last several days; the no-runner advice no longer tells people to run forge sync unless they changed the runner setting; command tests with a faked GitHub cover a long busy queue that then passes and a repo whose runner never picks anything up, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Functional. Doctor never diagnoses a missing runner from real GitHub check responses. The [check-runs API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs#list-check-runs-for-a-git-reference) does not expose a top-level `created_at`. Accessing it here raises KeyError, which is swallowed; `queued` remains false and the function returns before inspecting runner history. The passing proofs invent that field in tests/test_queued_checks_keep_waiting.py:54, tests/test_ci_waits_for_busy_runners.py:115 and tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py:124, masking the defect for both client histories. Use an available GitHub timestamp and make those fixtures reflect the actual response contract. This API-contract evidence is independent of the recorded ruling about bounded history sampling.
findings.title: Not done: doctor detects a runner that never picks anything up

findings.body: Raise: Functional. The new endpoint contains an unescaped `&`. src/forge/repo.py:118 passes it through subprocess without shell escaping, while tests/conftest.py:70 installs the fake GitHub CLI as `gh.cmd` on Windows. [Python documents](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/subprocess.html#security-considerations) that command scripts can undergo shell parsing even with shell=False. The query therefore splits into two commands: gh receives the endpoint without the date filter, and cmd attempts to execute `created=...`. Doctor reports a GitHub-access failure instead of the runner diagnosis, and the new diagnostic proofs fail in the Windows suite configured at .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:54–80. Preserve the complete query when passing through supported command shims.
findings.title: Preserve the history query through Windows command shims

stop.reason: Owner wants every in-flight fix finished; narrowed doctor's missing-runner diagnosis to one bounded rule: at most 100 workflow runs from the last 7 days, ignoring runs that ended successfully

why: v1.2.8's 'checks stayed queued for five minutes; no runner has picked them up' stop still fires when the organisation's shared runner pool is only busy (a client's checks queued behind other repos' runs, 2026-10-09), and its advice to run forge sync can't help; one repo can't tell a busy shared pool from a missing runner within five minutes
